THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. A Read has TWO ceilings — it
TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB — and BOTH HAVE ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE.
iter127 hit the byte ceiling (refused at 459 KB, 397 KB of it the `done` log); iter128 found the
TOKEN cap had been truncating unnoticed for longer, returning lines 1-43 of 92 and dropping five
fields.

TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT (corrected iter129): the tool prints "[Truncated: PARTIAL view]", so the
risk is an agent SKIMMING PAST it, not the tool hiding anything. The B/tok derivations moved to
method-notes.md at iter160; check_calibration owns them.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO
PLAN.md. It measures ALL THREE step-1 files, prints each one's HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates,
distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields, flags every other tools/loop file,
and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting. WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy
field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a short pointer behind. There are EIGHT precedents
— `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`, `methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`,
`spikesArchive`, `decisions._archive` (pointer INSIDE the field it drained) and `doneRecent` (drained
empty at 151; see `doneRecentNote`, do not refill) — each asserting its round-trip first. DO NOT DISCARD CONTENT TO MAKE THE
CHECK PASS: condensing prose you keep is fair payback, dropping archived text is not. WHEN IT TRIPS
ON GATES.md OR PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled
section, never drop one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.

M6 feature-complete. **ITER202: THE LEAD'S 19TH - THE ROW PATTERN DECIDING WHICH OPTIONS THE REFERENCE PAGE DOCUMENTS COULD NOT READ A BOLD ONE, A SHARED CELL OR A BARE ONE, AND THE FACT IT FEEDS WAS SILENT IN EXACTLY THAT DIRECTION.** Full account: done-archive.jsonl:203.

  201 left THREE sibling patterns; all three measured, **ONLY ONE UNSOUND**. `TableRowOption()` read ONE name per row, at the cell's very start, unemphasised, unindented. **THE TWO FACTS OVER IT ARE NOT SYMMETRIC:** declared-MINUS-tabled makes an unread row LOUDER (every REAL option protected - 36/36 rows match), but **tabled-MINUS-declared makes the set SMALLER, so a PHANTOM option never arrives** at the check whose message says a reader gets a parse error.

  **PRE 6/6:** a phantom in a bold span, one as the SECOND flag in a shared cell, one with no code span - EACH passed all 1460 tests; the same phantom spelt in pattern was CAUGHT (the denominator). Fixed in two halves: the reader takes a row's **FIRST CELL** and reads **every** code-spanned flag in it, plus **an assertion requiring the UNREAD SET to be EMPTY**. Blast radius measured before any C#: 36 -> 36, auditor empty. **POST 6/6**, incl. the bare-name cell caught by the NEW assertion and the real-option pair FLIPPING to GREEN. Verified: build 0/0; suite **1460 skipped=0**. **`EXPECTED_AT_LEAST` UNCHANGED - no new [Fact].**
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `python3 tools/loop/run-suite.py` BEFORE YOUR FIRST CHANGE AND AFTER YOUR LAST - NOT `dotnet test | tail`**, which drops the failure lines above the summary (154). **Expect 1460**; run-suite.py enforces that floor and reddens on an unparseable summary or a skip. A deliberate DROP means editing `EXPECTED_AT_LEAST` in the same commit, with the reason. Several tests sweep the tree's own PROSE outside `tests/`/`tools/`, so a docs-only edit - GATES.md too - can redden it, and **in C# a DOC COMMENT is prose**: reword it, **never widen a tripwire's count.** `dotnet test --nologo` RUNS ZERO TESTS AND EXITS 1 (172); one class is `--filter-query '/*/*/<Class>/*'`, **ONE pattern**.
**TWO MEASURED ITEMS ARE OPEN, NEITHER A TRACE. DO NOT RE-MEASURE.** (1) `publish --prune --dry-run` is NEVER INVOKED, exit code HOST-DEPENDENT (PruneGuard reads the CI vars before PublishCommand's `!dryRun`) - `--find 179`. (2) GREP CODES AND MESSAGE WORDS - a 403 test matches none of `Unauthorized|401|credential`, `--find 180`. **192: THE OTHER TWO WERE NOT DEFECTS** - the `ShippedRoots`/`NarrativeRoots` swaps, an ACCEPTED BAR per 186/187 (`--find 192`). **DO NOT 'FIX' THESE.**

**SEAMS SPENT, 157-198, DO NOT RE-PROBE:** every seam `run-harnesses.py`'s ten steps name (157-170), plus `RemoteBodyReadTests`, `ConsumerKnowledgeCoverageTests`, `ShippedRoots`, `InstructionRoots`, `SectionDirectories`, `SkippedTrees`, `ReaderFacing*`, `ShippedTree.Roots`/`Extensions`, `WorkflowTemplateTests`' `Templates` + 4 subsets, `ToolchainPinningTests`' scan bounds, `SkillContractTests`' `RestPaths`, `ChangelogTests`' six bounds, `CliReferencePageTests`' `PageWideOptions`, its `Instructional()`, `InvocationCarriers()`, `RootFiles()`' skip test and `SkippedDirectories` (199: all four fix pieces pinned one cell each), `IsPlaceholder()`'s FOUR BRANCHES + the option floor under them (200: 13 cells), `Invocation()`'s ARG CLASS and the escaped set under it (201: 15 cells) **and now `TableRowOption()` + the unread set under it, with its two sibling patterns bounded elsewhere (202: 6 cells; next paragraph has the reasons).** **CHECKED SOUND, DO NOT RE-CHECK: the eight at `--find 192`-`195`.** **196: `ChangelogTests.Plumbing` HAS NO TREE-DERIVABLE BOUND** - unguarded on purpose, its `remarks` says so. **DO NOT 'FIX' IT.**

**THE LEAD IS 19 FOR 19 AND PATTERN-AS-A-BOUND IS SPENT FOR THAT CLASS.** 202 fixed `TableRowOption()`: a bold span, a shared cell, a bare name and an indented row fell outside; the reader now takes a row's FIRST CELL and reads EVERY code-spanned flag in it, unread set asserted empty. **DO NOT RE-PROBE THE OTHER TWO - each bounded DIFFERENTLY, both measured at 202:** `CommandSection()` cannot under-match SILENTLY, because `The_reference_page_has_a_section_for_every_command_and_no_others` compares its key set to `docume --help`'s commands (an independent SET EQUALITY is a bound) and two facts index `sections[command]`; `OptionColumn()`'s input is MACHINE-GENERATED at two spaces (55 lines, 0 skipped), so no author's spelling reaches its excluded set. **202's OWN exclusions are load-bearing:** a row must OPEN with a `|` (needing only a pipe reads prose and piped examples as rows and INVENTS options) and a name is read only from a code span (a bare one reds via the unread set).

**NEXT, ONE LAYER UP, NOTICED AT 202 AND NOT PURSUED: A SPLIT DECIDES WHICH TEXT AN ASSERTION MAY BE SATISFIED BY.** `PageSections()` ends a body at the next `\n## ` OF ANY KIND, so a non-command h2 between two command sections would end a body early and take its option table out of BOTH directions at once; `PageWidePreamble()` splits the same page again at the FIRST such heading. Ask of any split: **which population does it decide, and what happens to the text falling BETWEEN two pieces of it?** **A PATTERN OR SPLIT THAT UNDER-MATCHES DOES NOT MISS, IT FABRICATES A SMALLER WORLD THAT PASSES** (166's 18 orphans). Method, THREE times proven: measure the population in python FIRST, one cell per branch at a site nothing else pins, a control that MUST be CAUGHT as the denominator, then assert the excluded set is EMPTY. **PAIR NARROW-TO-WIDE BY POSITION, NEVER zip()** (201). **MEASURE THE FIX'S BLAST RADIUS BEFORE WRITING THE C#** - 202's first draft indicted `|---|---|` and a piped invocation, both caught by the probe, neither by the suite. In order: **INCLUSION OR EXEMPTION?** (190/1); **WHO COVERS IT?** (192); **WHICH DIRECTION IS SILENT?** (193); **IS THE SIBLING BOUND DIFFERENTLY?** (196); **WHO COLLECTS?** (197/8). **RUN THE PRE PHASE BEFORE FINISHING THE DESIGN** - 198's overturned 3 of 6 - and **ASSERT THE PHASE: two snapshots, an unmutated total EQUALLING the floor.** **201: A CELL'S EXPECTED VERDICT IS PER-PHASE** - carry a `post_predict`, or POST prints CAUGHT-UNPREDICTED for every intended repair and **a verdict under the WRONG NAME costs the cell like one the grader cannot emit** (176). **A fact with several assertions does not say which fired in its NAME - read its words from the red log run-suite already kept.**

**BOOKKEEPING BEFORE run-harnesses.py (170 burned a ~7-min sweep).** A half-finished state.json fails six guards silently. Order: archive line, `doneCount`, the pair, THEN sweep - **never edit it mid-sweep, nor a file it BUILDS** (171/180).

**FIRST, RUN `git diff tools/loop/state.json` AND `git status`: AN ANSWER FROM MIRKO ARRIVES AS AN UNCOMMITTED EDIT TO THIS FILE** (155), **AND `git log --oneline -5` AGAINST `iteration`** (169). **Trust `decisions`/`gates` plus GATES.md's checkboxes over prose here; it can be flatly WRONG** (170).

**A GREEN LOCAL BUILD IS NOT A GREEN CI (169):** `gh run list --limit 3` on anything reaching origin. CI resolves a newer SDK and `AnalysisLevel: latest-recommended` follows it, so 0 warnings here can be N errors there (`decisions.analyzerBandDrift`). **DO NOT "FIX" IT** - ToolchainPinningTests asserts the hazard is STILL THERE. **origin/main is BEHIND**; no standing push authority. **`run-harnesses.py` is 10/10.** A product harness stays in `.mtk/` scratch, NOT `HARNESSES`.

**BUDGET: method-notes.md IS AT ~19,960 OF 20,000 TOKENS - ZERO. Do not force a note at the end of an iteration** (TWENTY-ONE owed since 179); funding one is its own increment, an INDEXING PASS - rotation and boilerplate are spent, the lever is REWRITING A STUB AS AN INDEX (173-177), and the size assertion belongs in the write script. **A generation 4 must be in BOTH `ARCHIVE_FILES` and `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS` in one change, and a replacement must not exceed what it replaces - both FAILING CHECKS.** **state.json HAS THE SAME SHAPE, and 201 measured the trap: two condensations that read like 700 B of payback netted 29 B**, because each carried a note about itself. **A stub costs what its headlines cost (170) - so drop the meta-commentary, not the content**, and re-run the checker after every attempt rather than estimating.

**EVERY REMAINING PLAN.md SS15 ITEM IS GATED ON MIRKO.**
**check-state-size.py RUNS TWELVE CHECKS**, nine refusing a vacuous pass. **FIVE DECLARED LISTS MUST BE EDITED IN THE SAME CHANGE AS WHAT THEY DECLARE:** `GATES_ARCHIVE_NON_GATE_KEYS`, `ARCHIVE_FILES`, `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS`, `CITATION_KNOWN_ABSENT`, **`HARNESSES`, paired BOTH ways with the runner's STEPS**. **SETTLING A BLOCKER IS A FOUR-PLACE EDIT (160), ROTATING A METHOD NOTE A THREE-PLACE ONE (166)**; only the archive body DESTROYS text if skipped. **A REFUSAL APPENDS, IT NEVER `return`s** (165). **DO NOT WRITE SPECIMEN PATHS IN PROSE** (167); the gitignored-.mtk ratchet.

**A CONSTANT IN PROSE IS A MIRROR.** `check_prose_constants` fails on a B/tok ratio neither live nor dated. **Live: 2.4 B/tok markdown, 2.3 JSON - never copy undated.** 198 MEASURED AND LEFT one: the sweep floor's two prose counts disagree (`132`, `146`; live 154 at 198, **higher since 199 added `src`**), all DATED, none load-bearing - the floor is `> 100`, and rewriting them mints a fresh mirror. **A count in prose goes stale the next time the population moves; the assertion carries a floor, not a number.**

**THEN CHECK GATES.md. NINE BOXES ARE UNCHECKED, ALL MIRKO'S** - five milestone gates, four side items, mirrored in `gates`; **the checker FAILS ON MIRROR OR STATUS DRIFT**. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver, m3, m4, m5, m2, m6. **EIGHT DECISIONS ARE OPEN, ALL FULLY MEASURED - what is left is a JUDGEMENT the loop must not make.** Settling `planSection5Deviations` empties `DeadFields.Places` - 192 covers that cliff.

**paste-format-on-edit-hook'S QUESTION IS SETTLED - DO NOT RE-ASK, DO NOT RECREATE `tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py`** (check #10 FAILS if it does). **The loop cannot write `.claude/`**: do not route around it - and 187 put `.claude/rules`+`references` UNDER A SWEEP, where a stale invocation is a red fixable only in `references/` (iter89). **docume-loop.sh CAN BE EDITED BUT CANNOT TAKE EFFECT** - the driver parsed its `while` on 2026-07-24. Live, re-read by path: ITERATION-PROMPT.md, loop-settings.json.

**MUTATION-HARNESS RULES: method-notes.md, read it whole.** **A HEREDOC THAT WRITES A FILE IS REFUSED**, as is an inline `python3 -c` with a `#` comment (178), a BASH `for` over `$f` (192) and **a QUOTED BRACE in inline python (197, twice more at 198 - use Edit)**: one-shot scripts under `.mtk/paths-<n>/`, loops in python. 170: a PARTIAL mutation grades the CHECK broken. 171: `rm -rf` DENIED, use `shutil.rmtree`. **173/175/176/177 ARE LIVE `##` SECTIONS THERE:** a build failure and a zero-test run both score GREEN (match `error [A-Z]+\d+` case-insensitively, assert the DENOMINATOR), revert via `git show HEAD:<file>`, PREDICT A SET NEVER A COUNT. **190/192: drive `dotnet build` YOURSELF first, THEN parse run-suite's stdout** - fully qualified ids, so match a predicted name by SUFFIX (198). **199: deleting a list entry with a trailing `//` comment ORPHANS IT - `SA1515` breaks the build and the cell grades NOTHING; anchor the WHOLE LINE.** Re-run one cell with `--only <name>` (it re-runs its own baseline); **169's refuse-on-dirty blocks your own POST phase - `--allow-dirty` keeps the BYTE snapshot (160)**. **198, at `--find 198`: `re.sub` with a FUNCTION repl takes the return LITERALLY** (one backslash, or you plant a regex matching NOTHING - **IDENTICAL FAILURE SETS ACROSS DIFFERENT MUTATIONS WERE THE TELL**). **In C#: `SA1122`, `SA1604`+`RCS1139`, CS1574, `SA1118` - method-notes' C# stub names each.** **174/178/180: a MISSED or GREEN cell can be the best finding; assert the anchor matched ONCE. 179: a RED cell failing EXACTLY ONE TEST is itself the finding. TWO NETS grades WRONG-TESTS and is GOOD (190).**

**191: `.mtk/suite-runs/` HOLDS ONLY REDS** (a green deletes its log), so a stale one looks concurrent - **date it against `git log -1 --format=%cd`, then `pgrep -fl`**.
**HYGIENE, DO NOT DELETE WITHOUT ASKING** (a data file): untracked `tests/golden/.claude/analytics.json` - ask Mirko: delete or gitignore? **FLAKES, WireMock, ONE SIGHTING EACH; TWICE IN A ROW IS A FIND** - SEVEN, `--find 185`; across 189-202's ~210 runs just TWO, at 194 and 202, **each cleared on re-run**. 202's (`CliDriftTests.The_whole_read_footprint...`) had ONE prior sighting, iter187 - NON-CONSECUTIVE, not a find.

blockers._archive: FULL BLOCKER BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/blockers-open.json (moved at iter139; nothing discarded, round-trip asserted — the eighth archive precedent, and like decisions._archive the pointer stays INSIDE the field it drained). Each line below is ONE OPEN blocker: what it is, whose call it is, and where to answer. EVERY ONE IS PHRASED AS A QUESTION FOR MIRKO and every one is also written up at length in GATES.md, which step 1 reads anyway — so open the archive only to ACT on one. TO ADD ONE, per protocol step 9: a short kebab-case key here with a ONE-LINE stub ending in a pointer, and the full body in blockers-open.json under the same key. TO SETTLE ONE, **FOUR PLACES, AND check-state-size.py NOW FAILS ON A HALF-EDIT**: delete the key from both, append a one-line verdict to blockersArchive.settled, AND append the body to blockers-archive.jsonl (line shape: `blockersArchive.format`). **THE FOURTH DESTROYS CONTENT IF SKIPPED** - iter155 skipped it. (Condensed iter150 as budget payback; the historical justification for the iter139 move is in blockers-open.json and the done archive.)
blockers.pushPolicy: OPEN, ITER121 — **may the loop push to origin/main?** The same question as `decisions.pushPolicy` in this file, which carries the numbers and the iter130 note; answer it THERE ("always", "on-request" or "never"). Blocks the remote half of gate-m5 and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading; blocks no offline work. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.rule-8-2a: OPEN, ITER75 — **may the §8.2a rule amendment be pasted?** One paste of tools/loop/rule-8-2a-paste.md into .claude/rules/git-workflow.md beneath §8.2. It scopes the force-push exception you already authorised (decisions.compositeAction: floating-v1) so a future iteration cannot read §8.2 literally and delete that work. The loop will not do it itself: it WIDENS force-push authority. Nothing waits on it. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json; full text GATES.md -> paste-rule-8-2a.
blockers.settings-corrections: OPEN, ITER131, TWO ONE-LINERS, NEITHER BLOCKING ANYTHING — (a) this workspace is untrusted (~/.claude.json hasTrustDialogAccepted:false), so three `.claude/settings.json` allow entries are ignored every iteration; zero cost today because --settings supplies a broader rule. (b) `Write(.env)` / `Write(.env.*)` in your GLOBAL settings enforce NOTHING — only `Edit(path)` rules are matched for file permissions. Both found by reading the CLI's own stderr, captured unread into every iteration log for 130 iterations. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.restart-loop-driver: OPEN, ITER139 — **will you restart the loop driver?** `touch tools/loop/STOP` -> wait for the pass to end -> `rm tools/loop/STOP` -> `./tools/loop/docume-loop.sh`. Bash parses a `while` loop once, so the process running since 2026-07-24 has never executed EITHER commit to docume-loop.sh since (7de6a86 was iter137's whole deliverable); tools/loop/MODEL is inert for the same reason. TESTED 9/9 at iter140: the code is correct and the only behaviour change is the model ID string, measured harmless. NOT blocking the pastes. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json; full instructions: GATES.md.

gates.gate-m2-aur-review: PENDING, MIRKO'S. The loop's half finished at iter113: 44 pages are up in DOCUMESBX. Needs your page-by-page review, then the tick. gates.gate-m3-approval-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the cheapest of the five: add ONE `approved` label to any published page ('CLI Reference', id 451969089, is a good one), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --labels`, republishes that page with `publish --notify-reviewers`, and you re-approve. `approvedBy` will read 'unknown' and that is correct, not a bug (spike S3: Confluence exposes no label author). THIS GATE ALSO GATES SHIPPED CODE - iter122's `--notify-reviewers` fires only where a run revokes an approval, and no DOCUMESBX page carries one, so nothing can exercise it live until this box moves.
gates.gate-m4-feedback-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S. Write ONE comment saying something factually wrong about a published page (an INLINE comment on a sentence exercises the most code), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --comments` -> `/docs-feedback` -> a `docs/feedback-<date>` PR -> republish -> `sync --reply`.
gates.gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and it is a DECISION not a task: does M5's §14 acceptance run on this repo (copy docs-drift-pr.yml in, add secrets) or fold into M7 where a real repo with real PRs exists? Answer in decisions.m5Acceptance. The live middle of the chain is already done and re-runnable (iter121: `drift --mark` labelled 9 of 11 sourced pages against DOCUMESBX and proved a label spends no page version).
gates.gate-m6-first-release: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the only irreversible one - a package on a GitHub Packages feed cannot be unpublished, which is why the loop will not do it. Steps: (1) confirm the three version carriers agree (Directory.Build.props, plugin.json, plugin/README.md's git-subdir ref; all read 0.1.0, and release.yml's first step refuses a mismatch before building, so a wrong guess costs nothing); (2) `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`; (3) drop README.md's 'Not published yet' note; (4) tick. The loop then walks the README literally in a fresh empty directory - that walk IS M6's acceptance - and needs a PAT with read:packages for the install half. Full steps: GATES.md.

decisions._archive: FULL DECISION BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/decisions-archive.json, moved there at iter130 because this field was 11.6 KB of the 50 KB that put step 1's Read past its budget. decisions.mermaidDialectGap: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter113 — **the JUDGEMENT is his; the FACTS were fully measured at iter156 and the loop must not pick an option.** beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 renders six families and nothing else. Do NOT 'repair' that by renumbering. check-state-size.py also checks ATTRIBUTION, COVERAGE and HEAD - the last would have caught iter132's loss when it happened.
